Science & Geography.question: 1) In which among the following, the speed of sound would be maximum?
Science & Geography.exp:
The speed of sound in a medium depends on the temperature of the medium. The speed of sound decreases when we go from solid to gaseous state.
In any medium as we increase the temperature the speed of sound increases. The speed of sound will be highest in humid air at 30°C.

Science & Geography.question: 2) Which among the following compounds is most commonly used in the Photochromic lenses?
Science & Geography.exp: Silver halides and most commonly silver Chloride is used in Photochromic lenses. But for plastic photochromic lenses, some organic products such as oxazines and naphthopyrans are used.

Science & Geography.question: 3) Which of the following is used in pencils?
Science & Geography.exp: Graphite is used in pencils.

Science & Geography.question: 4) What is the SI unit of acceleration due to gravity?
Science & Geography.exp: The acceleration due to gravity is the acceleration set up in the body when it falls freely under the effect of gravity alone. The SI unit of acceleration due to gravity is ms<sup>-2</sup>.

Science & Geography.question: 5) Which antigen is present in the O blood group?
Science & Geography.exp: There are no antigens present in Blood group O. It has both anti-A and anti-B antibodies in the plasma and also some special “anti-A,B” antibodies. Blood group AB has both A and B antigens, but no antibodies.

Science & Geography.question: 6) The gas usually filled in the electric bulb is-
Science & Geography.exp: Incandescent light bulbs are filled with an inert gas like nitrogen, argon, or krypton - so that the filament doesn't catch fire.

Science & Geography.question: 7) What is the value of the Triple point of water?
Science & Geography.exp: Triple point of water is the temperature at which ice, water and water vapours coexist. The value of the Triple point of water is 273.16 K. Kelvin is the S.I unit of Temperature represented by symbol K.

Science & Geography.question: 8) Galvanised iron sheets have a coating of
Science & Geography.exp: Galvanization is the process of applying a protective zinc coating to steel or iron in order to prevent it from rusting.

Science & Geography.question: 9) Which of the following parts of the eyes controls the size of the pupil?
Science & Geography.exp: The size of the pupil is controlled by the iris. The iris controls the amount of light entering into the eye.

Science & Geography.question: 10) Which of the gas is not known as green house gas?
Science & Geography.exp:
The list of GreenHouse Gases are as follows:
1) Water vapor
2) Carbon dioxide
3) Methane
4) Nitrous oxide
5) Ozone
6) Chlorofluorocarbons.
Hydrogen is not a GreenHouse Gas.

Science & Geography.question: 11) Soda water contains
Science & Geography.exp: Carbonated water or Soda water is water that has been infused with carbon dioxide gas under pressure. It is carbonic acid. This produces a bubbly drink that's also known as sparkling water, club soda, soda water, seltzer water and fizzy water. With the exception of seltzer water, they usually have salt added to improve the taste.

Science & Geography.question: 12) What is laughing Gas?
Science & Geography.exp: Nitrous oxide, commonly known as laughing gas or nitrous, is a chemical compound, an oxide of nitrogen with the formula N<sub>2</sub>O.

Science & Geography.question: 13) LPG consists of mainly:
Science & Geography.exp: Liquefied Petroleum Gas or LPG consists mainly of methane, propane, propylene, butane, and butylene in various mixtures. It is produced as a by-product of natural gas processing and petroleum refining. The components of LPG are gases at normal temperatures and pressures.

Science & Geography.question: 14) Air is a/an-
Science & Geography.exp: Air is a mixture because we can separate its components while in compounds we can not separate it.

Science & Geography.question: 15) Which of the following is the lightest metal?.
Science & Geography.exp: Lithium is the lightest metal of the following.

Science & Geography.question: 16) The time required by earth in 360 degree rotation to make a star return to the same position is called _____ day?
Science & Geography.exp:
The spinning of the earth on its polar axis in fact takes 23 hours, 56 minutes and 4.09 seconds for rotation through the 360 degree. This is called sidereal day.
During the time needed by the Earth to complete a rotation around its axis (a sidereal day), the Earth moves a short distance (approximately 1°) along its orbit around the sun.
So, after a sidereal day, the Earth still needs to rotate a small additional angular distance before the sun reaches its highest point. A solar day is, therefore, nearly 4 minutes longer than a sidereal day.

Science & Geography.question: 17) Which among the following is an area of evergreen forests?
Science & Geography.exp: The south east asia is the evergreen forest area.They have evergreen trees and have high rainfall as well. This is because they are located near the equator. There is no dry season in this area.

Science & Geography.question: ১৮) Puerto Rico Trench is located in which of the following oceans?
Science & Geography.exp: Puerto Rico Trench is the second deepest trench after Mariana trench

Science & Geography.question: 19) Which among the following countries is the world’s leading producer of synthetic industrial diamond?
Science & Geography.exp: China is the world’s leading producer of synthetic industrial diamonds. Industrial diamonds can be used in cutting, drilling, grinding, and polishing.

Science & Geography.question: 20) Which is the largest river system flowing to the Arctic Ocean?
Science & Geography.exp: The Yenisei River is the largest river system that flows to the Arctic Ocean. It is also the fifth longest river in the world. It flows through two countries i.e Mongolia and Russia.

Science & Geography.question: 21) Which of the following is the largest coral reef in the Atlantic Ocean?
Science & Geography.exp: The Mesoamerican Reef is the largest coral reef in the Atlantic Ocean. It is located in the Caribbean Basin. It is also known as the Great Mayan Reef and it is a World Heritage Site, too.

Science & Geography.question: 22) Which is the longest river in Asia?
Science & Geography.exp: The Yangtze River is the longest river in Asia. It is the third longest river in the world. It flows entirely within China. It is also the longest river in the world to flow within one country.

Science & Geography.question: 23) The Danube delta is a part of which among the following countries?
Science & Geography.exp: The Danube delta is the second largest river delta in Europe. The greater part of the Danube delta lies in Romania and a small part in Ukraine.

Science & Geography.question: 24) The sun reaches its maximum angular distance from the equator at the -
Science & Geography.exp: Since the ecliptic is tilted 23.5° with respect to the celestial equator, the Sun's maximum angular distance from the celestial equator is 23.5°. This happens at the solstices.

Science & Geography.question: 25) Which of the following is the International Date Line?
Science & Geography.exp: 180° longitude is the International Date line.

Science & Geography.question: 26) The Time of Cairo is 2 hours ahead of Greenwich time. Cairo is situated at -
Science & Geography.exp:
For every 1° longitude, there is a difference of 4 minutes.
For 2 hrs, there will be a difference of 30°.
So the correct answer is 30° east as Cairo is ahead of Greenwich time.

Science & Geography.question: 27) The Science of drawing map is called-
Science & Geography.exp: Cartography or map-making is the study and practice of crafting representations of the Earth upon a flat surface (see History of cartography), and one who makes maps is called a cartographer.

Science & Geography.question: 28) The World used to describe the shape of earth is-
Science & Geography.exp: Oblate Spheroid is a term that has been used to describe the shape of the Earth. The Earth is not a sphere.

Science & Geography.question: 29) Which planet in our solar system is nearly as big as Earth?
Science & Geography.exp: Venus is nearly as big as the Earth. As it is very similar to Earth in terms of size, average density, mass & surface gravity. It is also known as Earth's twin.

Science & Geography.question: 30) Which one of the following is a landlocked country?
Science & Geography.exp: Hungary is a landlocked country located on the Danube River Basin in Central Europe. It is bordered by Slovakia to the north, Ukraine to the northeast, Romania to the east, Croatia and Serbia & Montenegro to the south as well as Slovenia and Austria to the west.
